correctness.rationale: The proper NC6 order complex K has 130 vertices with rank multiplicities (15,50,50,15), exactly (130,1035,2160,1296) chains in dimensions 0..3, and covering homotopy ∨^{42}S³ by type-A EL-shellability. Rank-preserving rotation fixes every vertex of a stabilized chain, hence the geometric quotient admits genuine oriented orbit cells (26,177,360,216), not the orbit-poset order complex. Exhaustive signed boundaries satisfy ∂²=0. Integral ±1-pivot cancellations count (25,152,207), leaving chain modules (1,0,1,9) and a 1×9 degree-three-to-two matrix whose entries have gcd 3; a different independent greedy basis leaves ±3 entries rather than the source's single 3, but identical Smith diagonal 3. Therefore H2=Z/3,H3=Z^8,H1=0. Rotation by 2 and by 3 each fixes a proper partition, and together generate C6; Armstrong's orbit-space theorem on simply connected K gives π1=1. The simply connected 3-complex's 2-skeleton is a wedge of S², and integral SNF changes the 3-cell attaching maps to one degree-three map and eight null maps, yielding M(Z/3,2)∨∨⁸S³. Full finite enumeration is exhaustive for this specific six-point object, not extrapolated to all n.

value.rationale: This natural six-point exact torsion classification answers a nontrivial invariant for a canonical lattice under its natural sixfold symmetry. It identifies torsion created by a nonfree quotient of a torsion-free sphere wedge and distinguishes it from the larger dihedral and ordinary-partition quotients. Finite exact classifications can be valuable even without a general n result; this one is structurally motivated and not a database recomputation.
